slides.title: Principle
bullets: In photometric methods the component to be measured is turned into a compound that absorbs light, then the absorption of light by the solution is measured and the amount found from it.
A photometer is an optical instrument that measures light flux at fixed wavelengths; the photometric method is more objective and sensitive than the colorimetric one.

Light passes from the source through an entrance slit to a filter that transmits the required narrow spectrum, is partly absorbed in the cuvette, is turned into an electric signal in the photodetector and is measured by a microprocessor.

slides.title: Principle
bullets: The amount of light passing through the cuvette depends on the composition and amount of the substance in it.

slides.title: The instrument and where to put it
bullets: The manual describes the Screen Master (Hospitex Diagnostics) automatic photometer: six interference filters, a microcuvette and single-use cuvettes, temperature modes of 25, 30 and 37 °C.
Measuring modes: “end point”, “fixed time” and “kinetics”.

slides.title: The instrument and where to put it
bullets: The instrument stands in a clean room on a hard-surfaced desk, horizontal, away from direct sun and vibration, and away from air-conditioners, heaters and sources of strong electrical noise.
The mains cable is connected separately from other instruments where possible; the mains voltage is 220 V (±10%).

slides.title: The instrument and where to put it
bullets: For a long life the operating temperature should be 15–30 °C and the relative humidity 20–90%.
Before starting read the manual supplied with the instrument carefully.

slides.title: Manual determination: general order
bullets: 1. Prepare the working reagent according to the kit instructions (dissolve the dry substrate in the vial in the buffer).
2. Put working reagent, standard (calibrator) and sample into the cuvettes in the volumes in the instructions: separately for blank, standard and sample.
3. Mix gently and incubate at the stated temperature for the stated time.

slides.title: Manual determination: general order
bullets: 4. Set the wavelength, temperature and zero (against distilled water, air or reagent) as in the instructions; the cuvette light path is 1 cm.
5. Measure the absorbance; the calculation is the ratio of the sample absorbance to the standard, multiplied by the standard concentration.
6. If the result is beyond the limit of linearity the sample is diluted, the determination repeated and the result multiplied by the dilution.

slides.title: About absorbance
bullets: Most biochemical methods are designed for photometry in cuvettes with a 1 cm light path.
If the absorbance is 1, only 10% of the light passes through the solution and 90% is absorbed.
In all photometric instruments high accuracy is reached at an absorbance of about 0.3 — when half of the incident light passes.

slides.title: About absorbance
bullets: So a sample giving a very high absorbance is best diluted and measured again (see the linearity limit in the instructions).

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: If pipettes are mechanically damaged or the volume does not fit, the volumes will be inaccurate — do not use them.
The result is affected by inaccuracies in temperature, incubation time and dosing, and by breaches of the shelf life and storage rules; storing reagents above 37 °C sharply reduces their stability.
The water must be clean with a pH of 6.5–7.5; if in doubt take water from another source.
Do not work in scratched cuvettes; wipe the optical system; check the programme parameters and calibration.

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: Check a doubtful result with freshly prepared reagent or control material, and if possible on another instrument.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Some kit reagents are poisonous (for example the haemiglobincyanide reagent contains potassium cyanide); avoid skin and mucosal contact and follow the notes in the instructions.
Electrical instruments must be earthed; check the cable before connecting to the mains.
Reagents are “for in vitro diagnostic use only”.
